page: Amazon Web Services m5a.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The x86_64 architecture configuration supplies 8 vCPUs distributed across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. System memory totals 32.0 GB of DDR4 clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached storage options, and provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. Acceleration hardware such as GPUs is not included.

Performance benchmarks reflect the generational positioning of first-generation AMD EPYC silicon. In multi-threaded execution, the instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 6871.6 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2960.0, alongside 2360.94 in stress-ng multi-core testing. Single-threaded metrics are lower, recording 729.0 in Geekbench and 591.0 in stress-ng. Memory subsystems delivered 27.54 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 14.61 GB/sec for writes. Application-level tests demonstrate functional utility for data operations, delivering 4.98 million Redis SET operations per second and 5.01 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The hardware configuration provides a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring a solid 32 GB memory pool and balanced multi-threading without the cost overhead of newer CPU generations. Because single-threaded compute and memory bandwidth are constrained compared to newer hardware families, workloads that depend heavily on vector math or high single-core execution speed are not suitable. The instance is appropriate for standard enterprise workloads, including web application servers, containerized microservices, build nodes in CI/CD pipelines, and medium-scale caching or database services.
description: Amazon Web Services m5a.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz AMD EPYC 7571 x86_64 processor under the Nitro hypervisor. The configuration provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, adhering to a standard 1:4 CPU-to-RAM ratio. It lacks integrated local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing network-attached storage and offering a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate modest CPU and memory throughput, scoring 6871.6 in PassMark CPU and 2960.0 in Geekbench multi-core. In memory and caching tests, it achieved 4.98 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread performance is limited by older EPYC architecture, the instance provides cost-efficient multi-threaded compute and stable memory capacity. It is suitable for general application hosting, web servers, continuous integration tasks, and mid-tier backend services.
